results.title: Koebe quarter theorem

results.title: The boundary of a normalized univalent image of the disc is within distance one of the origin
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The boundary of a normalized univalent image of the disc is within distance one of the origin. Let $D=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the unit disk and suppose $f:D\to\mathbb{C}$ is an injective holomorphic function with $f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=1$. Let $\Omega=f(D)$ and let $\partial\Omega$ be its boundary. Then $\mathrm{dist}(0,\partial\Omega)=\inf\{|z|:z\in\partial\Omega\}\le 1$.

results.title: Comparison principle for the Dirichlet problem on $(0, 1)$

results.title: Domination states

results.summary: A domination state is one of three labels: uncovered, covered or occupied.

results.title: Domination polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite graph $G$, the domination polynomial of $G$ is the polynomial $\sum_S z^{|S|}$ with integer coefficients, the sum running over the dominating sets $S$ of $G$.

results.title: Domination state of a vertex
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph, $S$ a finite set of vertices of $G$ and $v$ a vertex of $G$. The domination state of $v$ relative to $S$ in $G$ is occupied if $v \in S$, covered if $v \notin S$ and $v$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex of $S$, and uncovered otherwise.

results.title: Domination signature
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$ (the row). A map $\sigma$ assigning to each vertex of $V$ a domination state (uncovered, covered or occupied) is a signature for $R$ if no uncovered vertex is adjacent in $R$ to an occupied vertex: for all vertices $i, j$ adjacent in $R$, it is not the case that $\sigma(i)$ is uncovered and $\sigma(j)$ is occupied.

results.title: Signatures of a row graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $R$ on a vertex set $V$ (the row), a signature of $R$ is a map $\sigma$ assigning to each vertex of $V$ a domination state (uncovered, covered or occupied) such that $\sigma$ is a domination signature for $R$, that is, no uncovered vertex is adjacent in $R$ to an occupied vertex. This is the type of all signatures of $R$; when $R$ is a cycle they are the paper's cyclic signatures.

results.title: All-covered signature
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a graph $R$ (the row), the all-covered signature $\sigma_\bullet$ of $R$ is the signature that gives every vertex of $R$ the state covered; it is a signature because it has no uncovered vertex.

results.title: Number of occupied vertices
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set and let $\sigma$ assign a domination state (uncovered, covered or occupied) to each element of $V$. The occupied count $\operatorname{occ}(\sigma)$ is the number of elements $i \in V$ such that $\sigma(i)$ is occupied.

results.title: Domination transfer matrix

results.title: A vertex is occupied exactly when it lies in the set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph, $S$ a finite set of vertices of $G$ and $v$ a vertex of $G$. Then the domination state of $v$ relative to $S$ in $G$ is occupied if and only if $v \in S$.

results.title: Dominating sets have no uncovered vertex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $S$ a finite set of vertices of $G$. Then $S$ dominates $G$ if and only if no vertex of $G$ has domination state uncovered relative to $S$ in $G$.

results.title: The domination polynomial at one counts dominating sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite graph $G$, the value at $1$ of the domination polynomial of $G$ equals the number of dominating sets of $G$.

results.title: The all-covered signature has no occupied vertex
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every simple graph $R$ on a finite vertex set, the number of occupied vertices of the all-covered signature of $R$ is $0$.

results.title: Grid domination polynomial as a sum of almost dominating polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $n$, let $P_k$ denote the path on the vertices $0, \dots, k - 1$. Then the domination polynomial of the grid $P_m \mathbin{\square} P_{n+1}$ equals $\sum_\sigma G^\sigma(z)$, the sum running over the signatures $\sigma$ of the row graph $P_m$ with no uncovered vertex, where $G^\sigma(z)$ is the almost dominating polynomial of $P_m$ with $n + 1$ rows and last-row state $\sigma$.

results.title: Transfer-matrix formula for the domination polynomial of the torus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $n$ with $n \ge 1$, let $C_k$ denote the cycle graph on the vertices $0, \dots, k - 1$, in which distinct $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $i - j \equiv \pm 1 \pmod k$, and let $\bar A$ be the domination transfer matrix of the row graph $C_m$. Then the domination polynomial of the torus $C_m \mathbin{\square} C_n$ equals the trace of $\bar A^n$.

results.title: First integral of the Lotka–Volterra system
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Lotka–Volterra first integral `V(x, y) = δ x - γ log x + β y - α log y` for the system `x' = α x - β x y`, `y' = δ x y - γ y`. It is meaningful on the open positive quadrant `x, y > 0`; elsewhere `Real.log` takes junk values (`log 0 = 0`, `log (-x) = log x`).

results.title: Lotka–Volterra first integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `x' = α x - β x y` and `y' = δ x y - γ y` at time `t` and `x t, y t > 0`, then `t ↦ V(x t, y t)` has derivative `0` at `t`.

results.title: Positive solutions lie on level curves
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `(x, y)` solves the Lotka–Volterra system on `[0, ∞)` and both populations stay positive there, then `V(x t, y t) = V(x 0, y 0)` for all `t ≥ 0`.

results.title: The coexistence equilibrium minimizes the first integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For positive parameters and `x, y > 0`, `V(γ / δ, α / β) ≤ V(x, y)`.
